en: Using or exercising caution; careful; tentative

ex.en: He is too cautious to try anything new.
ex.ja: 彼はあまりに用心深いため、新しいことは何も試せない。

ex.en: You should be cautious of how you laugh.
ex.ja: 笑い方に注意すべきである。

ex.en: He is cautious of his actions.
ex.ja: 彼は行動が慎重だ。

note.ja: caution（用心）+ -ous。ラテン語 cavere（用心する）。「用心深い・慎重な」。

en: One holding the lowest rank in most Commonwealth police forces. (See also chief constable.)
A police officer or an officer with equivalent powers.

constable.ety: From Middle English constable, cunstable, constabil, connestable, cunestable, from Old French conestable, from Latin comes stabulī (“officer of the stables”). For the sense-development; compare marshal. Doublet of connétable.

note.ja: ラテン語 comes stabuli（厩舎の長）から。「馬小屋の長」→ 王家の高官 →「巡査」。stable（馬小屋）と同じ。

en: To work or act together, especially for a common purpose or benefit.
To allow for mutual unobstructed action.

cooperate.ety: Originated 1595–1605 from Late Latin cooperātus, perfect passive participle of cooperor (“to work with”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix) for more. Equivalent to co- + operate. Displaced native Old English efnwyrċan.

ex.en: Cooperate with your friends in doing the work.
ex.ja: その仕事をするの友人と協力しなさい。

ex.en: We had to cooperate with each other.
ex.ja: 私たちは互いに協力せざるを得なかった。

ex.en: I cooperated with my sister in cleaning the room.
ex.ja: 私は姉と協力して部屋を掃除した。

note.ja: co（共に）+ operari（働く）。「協力する」。operate と同じ。

en: A professional who counsels people, especially on personal problems.
A school counselor, often in a specialty such as careers, education, or health.

counselor.ety: From Middle English counseilour, counseiler, from Anglo-Norman cunseiler, from Old French conseillier, from Latin cōnsiliārius, agent noun from cōnsilior (“to take counsel”), from cōnsilium (“plan, council, wisdom, advice”). Compare councilor. Displaced native Middle English redere, Middle English redesman, and Middle English redyeve, from Old English rǣdġiefa (literally “advice giver”).

note.ja: counsel（助言）+ -or。ラテン語 consilium（相談）。「相談に乗る人」→「カウンセラー・相談員」。consult と同系。

en: A concrete margin along the edge of a road; a kerb (UK, Australia, New Zealand).
A raised margin along the edge of something, such as a well or the eye of a dome, as a strengthening.
To check, restrain or control.
To rein in.

curb.ety: From Middle French courbe (“curve, curved object”), from Latin curvus (“bent, crooked, curved”). Doublet of curve.

ex.en: Please give me some kind of medicine to curb the pain.
ex.ja: 痛みを抑える薬を何かください。

ex.en: The government should endeavor to curb inflation.
ex.ja: 政府はインフレ抑制に努力すべきだ。

ex.en: A boy is taking his sweet time pushing the cart toward the curb.
ex.ja: 男の子が縁石の方へカートをゆっくり押しやっている。

note.ja: ラテン語 curvus（曲がった）から。馬の口に付ける湾曲した鎖 →「抑制する」、道の端を区切る石 →「縁石」。curve と同じ。

en: An action or act; something that is done.
A brave or noteworthy action; a feat or exploit.
To transfer real property by deed.

deed.ety:
From Middle English dede, from Old English dēd, dǣd (“deed, act”), from Proto-West Germanic *dādi, from Proto-Germanic *dēdiz (“deed”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰéh₁tis (“deed, action”). Analyzable through Proto-Germanic as do + -th. Doublet of thesis.
The real estate sense derives from the fact that property deeds are traditionally used to demonstrate proof of ownership of a legal title in common law jurisdictions, such as England & Wales and most of the United States.
Cognates
Cognate with West Frisian died, Dutch daad (“deed, act”), German Low German Daad, German Tat (“deed, action”), Swe

ex.en: She is honest in deeds and in words.
ex.ja: 彼女は行動も言葉も誠実だ。

ex.en: The will is as good as the deed.
ex.ja: 何事をするにも志が大切。

ex.en: There is absolutely nothing wrong with his deed.
ex.ja: 彼の行為にはまったく悪いところはない。

note.ja: 古英語 dǣd（行い）から。do（する）と同じ祖先。「行い」→ 行いを記した書類 →「（不動産の）証書」。

en: Confined to a predetermined fate or destiny; certain.

ex.en: My mother will be destined to say no.
ex.ja: うちの母はノーと言うに決まっている。

ex.en: He was destined never to meet her again.
ex.ja: 彼は２度と彼女に会えないよう運命づけられていた。

ex.en: We will arrive at the destined station shortly.
ex.ja: もうすぐ目的の駅に着く。

note.ja: destine（運命づける）+ -ed。「運命づけられた」→「〜行きの」。destination と同じ。

en: Not physically attached; separated from something to which it could connect.
Of a house: not joined to another house on either side.

note.ja: detach（引き離す）+ -ed。attach の対。「分離した」→ 他と離れた「一戸建ての」→「超然とした」。

en: In an efficient manner.

efficiently.ety:
Etymology tree
English efficient
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English efficiently
From efficient + -ly.

ex.en: If you make a study plan, you can make progress efficiently.
ex.ja: 勉強の計画を立てておくと、効率よく進められる。

ex.en: The office staff worked quickly and efficiently to resolve the problem.
ex.ja: 事務所の職員は迅速かつ効率的に働いて、その問題を解決した。

ex.en: Your response is greatly appreciated and will enable us to prepare more efficiently.
ex.ja: お返事をお待ちしております。またお返事をいただくことにより、私どもはより効率よく会議の準備をすることができます。

note.ja: efficient（効率のよい）+ -ly。ex（外へ）+ facere（作る）。「成果を作り出す」→「効率よく」。effect と同じ。

en: The act of encouraging
Something that incites, supports, promotes, protects or advances; incentive

ex.en: Without your encouragement, I would've given up this plan.
ex.ja: あなたの激励がなかったら、この計画は諦めていたでしょうね。

ex.en: Your words of encouragement meant a lot to me.
ex.ja: あなたの激励の言葉に励まされました。

ex.en: Your encouragement will draw her out.
ex.ja: あなたが勇気づけてやれば彼女は自由に話すでしょう。

note.ja: en（〜にする）+ courage（勇気）+ -ment。「勇気を与えること」→「励まし」。courage はラテン語 cor（心）。

en: A group of people, especially within a political organization, which expresses a shared belief or opinion different from people who are n…
Strife; discord.

faction.ety: Borrowed from Middle French faction, from Latin factiō (“a group of people acting together, a political faction”), noun of process from perfect passive participle factus, from faciō (“do, make”). Doublet of fashion.

ex.en: The two factions gang up with each other.
ex.ja: ２つの派閥が手をむすんだ。

ex.en: The two factions joined forces.
ex.ja: ２つの派閥が手をむすんだ。

ex.en: He once belonged to the Fukuda faction.
ex.ja: 彼は福田派に属していました。

note.ja: ラテン語 factio（行うこと・党派）から。fac（する）。一緒に行動する集団 →「派閥・党派」。

Supporting the principles of fascism.
A proponent of fascism.

note.ja: イタリア語 fascista から。fascio（束）。古代ローマの権威の象徴「束ねた棒（fasces）」から。

en: A branching, hair-like structure that grows on the bodies of birds, used for flight, swimming, protection and display.
Long hair on the lower legs of a dog or horse, especially a draft horse, notably the Clydesdale breed. Narrowly only the rear hair.
To cover or furnish with feathers; (when of an arrow) to fletch.
To adorn, as if with feathers; to fringe.

feather.ety:
From Middle English fethere, from Old English feþer, from Proto-West Germanic *feþru, from Proto-Germanic *feþrō, from Proto-Indo-European *péth₂r̥ (“feather, wing”), from *peth₂- (“to fly”).
Cognate with West Frisian fear (“feather”), Cimbrian bèdara, fòdara (“pillowcase”), vèdara (“feather”), Dutch veder, veer (“feather”), German Feder (“feather”), German Low German Fedder (“feather”), Luxembourgish Fieder (“feather”), Vilamovian faoder (“feather”), Yiddish פֿעדער (feder, “feather”), Danish fjeder, fjer (“feather”), Faroese fjøður (“feather”), Icelandic fjöður (“feather”), Norwegian Bokmål f

ex.en: The bird was covered with white feathers.
ex.ja: その鳥は白い羽に覆われていた。

ex.en: He is always busy feathering his own nest.
ex.ja: 彼は私腹を肥やすのに余念がない。

ex.en: Fine feathers make fine birds.
ex.ja: 立派な羽が立派な鳥をつくる。

note.ja: 古英語 fether から。ギリシャ語 pteron（翼）と同じ祖先。helicopter の -pter も同じ。

en: Something that is fixed in place, especially a permanent appliance or other item of personal property that is considered part of a house …
A regular patron of a place or institution; a person constantly present at a certain place.
To furnish with, as, or in a fixture.
To schedule (a match).

fixture.ety: Alteration of older fixure, on the model of mixture.

note.ja: fix（固定する）+ -ure。「固定された備品」→ 定着した人・物 →（英）日程が固定された「試合予定」。

en: A bet or wager.
A significant risk, undertaken with a potential gain.
To take a risk, with the potential of a positive outcome.
To play risky games, especially casino games, for monetary gain.

gamble.ety: From earlier gamel, from Middle English *gamlen, *gamelen, variant of Middle English gamenen, from Old English gæmnian, gamnian, gamenian (“to joke; play”), related to Old English gamen (“joy; mirth; pleasure; entertainment; pastime; sport; game”), equivalent to game + -le. Compare Old Danish gammel, Middle High German gamel (“pleasure; fun”). More at game.

ex.en: I understand that this is a gamble.
ex.ja: これが博打だってことは分かってます。

ex.en: You must not gamble at cards.
ex.ja: トランプで賭けてはいけない。

ex.en: He gambled on the war coming to an early end.
ex.ja: 彼は戦争が早々と終わるとあてこんでいた。

note.ja: 古英語 gamenian（遊ぶ）から。game と同じ。「賭け事をする」。

en: A designated player that attempts to prevent the opposing team from scoring by protecting a goal.

goalkeeper.ety:

Proto-West Germanic *gailu

Middle English gol
English goal
English keeper
English goalkeeper
From goal + keeper.

ex.en: Who is the goalkeeper?
ex.ja: ゴールキーパーは誰なの？

note.ja: goal（ゴール）+ keeper（守る人）。「ゴールを守る人」。

en: A child of someone's child.

ex.en: An old man sat surrounded by his grandchildren.
ex.ja: 老人が孫たちに囲まれて座っていた。

ex.en: My great-grandchild is eight years old.
ex.ja: ひ孫は八歳ですよ。

ex.en: He sat surrounded by his grandchildren.
ex.ja: 彼は孫達に囲まれて座っていました。

note.ja: grand（一世代離れた）+ child（子）。「孫」。

en: Incapable of causing harm or danger; safe.
Not intended to harm; inoffensive.

harmless.ety:
From Middle English harmles, from Old English *hearmlēas, from Proto-Germanic *harmalausaz (“without harm; harmless”), equivalent to harm + -less.
Cognate with German harmlos (“harmless”), Danish harmløs (“harlmess”), Swedish harmlös (“harmless”).

ex.en: This is harmless in itself.
ex.ja: これは本来無害です。

ex.en: Heat will break this chemical down into harmless gases.
ex.ja: 熱がこの化学薬品を無害な気体に分解するだろう。

ex.en: Most snakes on this island are harmless.
ex.ja: この島ではたいていのヘビは無害である。

note.ja: harm（害）+ -less。「害のない」。

To stammer; to falter in speaking.

ex.en: Don't hesitate to ask your teacher a question.
ex.ja: 質問があったら、遠慮しないで先生に聞きなさい。

ex.en: Tom said that Mary hesitated to do that.
ex.ja: メアリーはそうするのを躊躇したとトムは言った。

ex.en: Please don't hesitate to ask me any questions.
ex.ja: どんな質問でも遠慮なく私に聞いてください。

note.ja: ラテン語 haerere（くっつく）から。hes + itate。足が地面にくっつく →「ためらう」。adhere（くっつく）も同じ。

en: Feeling hope
Inspiring hope
Someone who is hoping for success or victory, especially as a candidate in a political election.

hopeful.ety:

From hope + -ful.

ex.en: This book tells that life is hopeful.
ex.ja: この本を読めば、人生は希望に満ちていることが分かる。

ex.en: Spring makes us hopeful about the future.
ex.ja: 春は私たちに未来への希望を抱かせる。

ex.en: I feel hopeful about the future.
ex.ja: 私は将来に希望を持っている。

note.ja: hope（希望）+ -ful。「希望に満ちた」→「有望な」。

en: Of, from, or pertaining to present-day Hungary, the ethnic Hungarian people or the Hungarian language.
Of, from, or pertaining to the Kingdom of Hungary, during the days of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, regardless of ethnicity.
A person from present-day Hungary or of ethnic Hungarian descent.
The main language of Hungary.

ex.en: "Why are you studying Hungarian?" "Because it's there."
ex.ja: 「なぜ、ハンガリー語を勉強してるの？」「そこにあるからさ」

ex.en: The Hungarian flag is red, white, and green.
ex.ja: ハンガリーの国旗は、赤・白・緑です。

ex.en: Hungarian is a very beautiful language.
ex.ja: ハンガリー語って、すごく綺麗な言葉なのよ。

note.ja: Hungary + -an。中世の民族名 Ungri から。

en: The science of health, its promotion and preservation.
Those conditions and practices that promote and preserve health.

hygiene.ety: From French hygiène, from Ancient Greek ὑγιεινή (τέχνη) (hugieinḗ (tékhnē), literally “art of health”), from ὑγιεινός (hugieinós, “of health, good for the health, wholesome, sound, healthy”), from ὑγιής (hugiḗs, “healthy, sound”).

ex.en: She studies hygiene as part of her domestic science course.
ex.ja: 彼女は家政学の一部として衛生学を学んでいる。

note.ja: ギリシャ神話の健康の女神 Hygieia から。hygiēs（健康な）。「衛生」。

en: Existing only in the imagination.
Relating or belonging to the imagination.
Imagination; fancy.
An imaginary number.

imaginary.ety:
From Middle English ymaginarie, ymagynary, from Latin imāginārius (“relating to images, fancied”), from imāgō, equivalent to imagine + -ary.
The mathematical sense derives from René Descartes's use (of the French imaginaire) in 1637, La Geometrie, to ridicule the notion of regarding non-real roots of polynomials as numbers. Although Descartes' usage was derogatory, the designation stuck even after the concept gained acceptance in the 18th century.

ex.en: All the characters in this book are imaginary.
ex.ja: この本のすべての登場人物は想像上のものです。

ex.en: All the events described in this story are imaginary.
ex.ja: この物語の中で書かれているすべての出来事は架空のものです。

ex.en: You didn't really see a ghost—it was only imaginary.
ex.ja: あなたは本当に幽霊を見たのではない。それは架空のものでしかなかったのだ。

note.ja: imagine（想像する）+ -ary。ラテン語 imago（像）。「想像上の」。imaginative（想像力豊かな）と区別。

ex.en: Mary was wrongly imprisoned for nearly 10 years.
ex.ja: メアリーは、10年近くの間、不当に投獄されていました。

en: An educational institution for young children, usually between ages 4 and 6; a nursery school.
The elementary school grade before first grade.

kindergarten.ety: Unadapted borrowing from German Kindergarten (“kindergarten”, literally “garden of children”), coined by German pedagogue Friedrich Fröbel in 1840.

ex.en: I learned that when I was in kindergarten.
ex.ja: それ習ったの、私が幼稚園の時だよ。

ex.en: Tom and I've been friends since kindergarten.
ex.ja: トムとは幼稚園の時からの友達なんだ。

ex.en: Now, now, eat quickly, you have to go to kindergarten.
ex.ja: ほらほら、早く食べて幼稚園行かなきゃ。

note.ja: ドイツ語 Kinder（子どもたち）+ Garten（庭）。「子どもの庭」→「幼稚園」。19世紀のドイツの教育者フレーベルの造語。

en: In a loud manner; at a high volume.
In a loud manner; gaudily, showily.

loudly.ety: From Middle English loudly, equivalent to loud + -ly.

ex.en: Please speak loudly, so I can hear you.
ex.ja: 大きい声で話してくださると聞こえるのですが。

ex.en: Could you speak a little less loudly?
ex.ja: もう少し小さな声でお願いできますか？

ex.en: You had better not speak loudly in this room.
ex.ja: この部屋では大声で話さないほうがよい。

note.ja: loud（大声の）+ -ly。「大声で」。

From Middle English mekanyk (“mechanical”), from Old French mecanique, from Latin mechanicus (“of or belonging to machines or mechanics, inventive”), from Ancient Greek μηχανικός (mēkhanikós, “pertaining to machines or contrivance, mechanic, ingenious, inventive”), from μηχανή (mēkhanḗ, “a mac

ex.en: Take it to a mechanic, and get it fixed.
ex.ja: 修理所に行って修理してもらってください。

ex.ja: 整備士ではないんですね？

ex.en: You're not a mechanic, are you?
ex.ja: 整備士ではないんですね？

en: To fail to care for or attend to something.
To omit to notice; to forbear to treat with attention or respect; to slight.
The act of neglecting.
The state of being neglected.

neglect.ety: The verb is inherited from Middle English neglect, neclect, derived from Latin neglēctus, perfect passive participle of neglegō (“to make light of, disregard, not to pick up”), itself from nec (“not”) + legō (“to pick up, select”). The noun is from neglēctus (“neglect”). First attested in 1460, the noun in 1588.

ex.en: That old house has been neglected for years.
ex.ja: その古い家は何年もほっておかれている。

ex.en: You must account for your neglect of duty.
ex.ja: 君は職務怠慢の申し開きをしなければならない。

ex.ja: 君はパンを買ってくるように私に言うのを怠った。

en: Of or pertaining to the northwest; from or to in such a direction.
Blowing from that direction.
A film or other dramatic work set primarily in the late 19th or early 20th century in the northwest of North America.

northwestern.ety: Probably the reflex of Old English *norþwesterne, equivalent to north + western, cognate with or formed similarly to Middle Low German nōrtwestern and Old High German nordwestrōni. Compare earlier northeastern, southeastern, and southwestern.

ex.en: "Is this Arabic?" "No, it's Uyghur - a language that's spoken in northwestern China."
ex.ja: 「これはアラビア語ですか？」「いいえ、それはウイグル語といって、中国の北西部で話されている言語です」

note.ja: north（北）+ west（西）+ -ern。「北西の」。

en: One who gives or causes offense, or does something wrong.
A person who commits an offense against the law, a lawbreaker.

offender.ety: From Middle English offendour, offender, offendir, equivalent to offend + -er.

ex.en: Sometimes first offenders are in need of help.
ex.ja: 初犯者には、ときに助けが必要だ。

ex.en: The more laws, the more offenders.
ex.ja: 法律が多ければ多いほど、違反者も多くなる。

ex.en: Such conduct would subject the offender to a heavy penalty.
ex.ja: そのような行いをすれば違反者は重罰を受けるだろう。

note.ja: offend（罪を犯す・感情を害する）+ -er。ob（〜に向かって）+ fendere（打つ）。「違反者」。defend と同じ fend。

en: The exercise of authority or power in a burdensome, cruel, or unjust manner.
The act of oppressing, or the state of being oppressed.

oppression.ety: From Middle English oppression, from Old French oppression, from Latin oppressiō (“a pressing down, violence, oppression”), from opprimō; see oppress.

ex.en: They rose against oppression.
ex.ja: 彼らは圧制に反抗して立った。

ex.en: Ethnic minorities struggle against prejudice, poverty, and oppression.
ex.ja: 少数民族は偏見、貧困、抑圧と戦っている。

ex.en: The slaves suffered cruel oppression.
ex.ja: 奴隷たちは残酷な抑圧に苦しんでいた。

note.ja: op（〜に向かって）+ press（押す）+ ion。押さえつけること →「抑圧・圧迫」。

en: Inspired by or showing patriotism; done out of love of one's country; zealously and unselfishly devoted to the service of one's country
A postage stamp, Civil War token, etc. bearing a patriotic design.

patriotic.ety: From French patriotique, from Late Latin patriōticus, from Ancient Greek πατριωτικός (patriōtikós), from πατριώτης (patriṓtēs), equivalent to patriot + -ic.

ex.en: Let's sing a patriotic air.
ex.ja: 愛国的な歌を１曲歌おう。

ex.en: Let's sing a patriotic song.
ex.ja: 愛国的な歌を１曲歌おう。

note.ja: patriot（愛国者）+ -ic。ギリシャ語 patris（祖国）、patēr（父）。「父祖の地を愛する」。paternal と同じ。

en: One who pitches (in any sense) anything
The player who delivers the ball to the batter.

ex.en: I dropped the pitcher and it broke.
ex.ja: ピッチャーを落として割っちゃった。

ex.en: The handle of the pitcher was broken.
ex.ja: 水差しの取っ手が壊れた。

ex.en: The coach made him a good pitcher.
ex.ja: そのコーチが彼を名選手にした。

note.ja: 「投手」は pitch（投げる）+ -er。「水差し」は古フランス語 pichier からで別語。

en: A large open space for children to play in, usually having dedicated play equipment (such as swings and slides).
Any physical or metaphysical space in which a person or organization has free rein to do as they please.

playground.ety: From play + ground. Compare Middle English playstede (“playground”) from Old English pleġstede.

ex.en: I saw them play baseball in the playground.
ex.ja: 彼らが運動場で野球をするのを見た。

ex.en: There was no student in the playground.
ex.ja: グラウンドにはひとりの生徒もいなかった。

ex.en: Tom, Mary and John were playing tag on the playground.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーとジョンは、運動場で鬼ごっこをして遊んでいた。

note.ja: play（遊ぶ）+ ground（地面）。「遊び場・校庭」。

en: That has, or is supplied with, inhabitants or content.

ex.en: The South East region of England is densely populated.
ex.ja: 英国の南東区は人口密度が高い。

ex.en: What's New Zealand like? Is it as sparsely populated as Australia?
ex.ja: ニュージーランドはどんな所ですか。オーストラリアと同じように人口が散在していますか。

note.ja: populate（住む）+ -ed。ラテン語 populus（民衆）。「人が住んでいる」。

en: An adverse judgment or opinion formed beforehand or without knowledge of the facts.
A preconception, any preconceived opinion or feeling, whether positive or negative.
To have a negative impact on (someone's position, chances etc.).
To cause prejudice in; to bias the mind of.

prejudice.ety: From Middle English prejudice, from Old French prejudice, derived from Latin praeiūdicium (“previous judgment or damage”), from prae- (“before”) + iūdicium (“judgment”).

ex.en: I don't have a prejudice against foreign workers.
ex.ja: 外国人労働者に偏見は持っていません。

ex.en: He will never get anywhere with that prejudiced idea.
ex.ja: そんな偏見を持っていると決してうまくいかない。

ex.en: He had a prejudice against women drivers.
ex.ja: 彼は女性ドライバーに偏見を抱いていた。

note.ja: pre（前もって）+ judic（裁く）+ e。前もって裁くこと →「偏見」。jud は jus（法）+ dic（言う）。

en: Likely or most likely to be true.
Likely to happen.
Something that is likely.
A person who is likely to appear or do a certain thing.

probable.ety: From Middle English probable, from Old French probable, from Latin probābilis (“that may be proved, credible”), from probāre (“to test, examine”); see probe, probity, prove. Compare recent doublet provable.

ex.en: A telephone call from him is probable tonight.
ex.ja: 今晩きっと彼から電話がかかるだろう。

ex.en: It is probable that she will come tomorrow.
ex.ja: 明日彼女が来るというのはありそうなことだ。

ex.en: It is probable that he forgot about it.
ex.ja: たぶん彼はそのことを忘れたのだろう。

note.ja: prob（試す・証明する）+ able。証明できそうな →「ありそうな・見込みのある」。

en: A period of time when a person occupies a position only conditionally and may be removed if certain conditions are not met.
A type of sentence where convicted criminals are permitted to continue living in a community but will automatically be sent to jail if th…

probation.ety: Inherited from Middle English probacioun, from Middle French probation, from Old French probacion, from Latin probatio (“a trying, inspection, examination”), from probare, past participle probatus (“to test, examine”); see probate, probe, prove.

ex.en: The end of my probation period is nearing.
ex.ja: 私の試用期間は終わりに近づいてきている。

note.ja: prob（試す）+ ation。試すこと →「試用期間・執行猶予・保護観察」。

en: Something which projects, protrudes, juts out, sticks out, or stands out.
The action of projecting or throwing or propelling something.

projection.ety: From either the Middle French projection or its etymon, the Classical Latin prōiectiō (stem: prōiectiōn-), from prōiciō, equivalent to project + -ion. Compare the Modern French projection, the German Projektion, and the Italian proiezione.

ex.en: I have to submit sales projections twice a quarter.
ex.ja: 四半期に２度、販売計画書を提出しなければならない。

ex.en: Let's begin practicing voice projection.
ex.ja: まず発声練習から始めましょう。

note.ja: project（投影する）+ -ion。pro（前へ）+ jacere（投げる）。「前に投げること」→「投影・予測・突出部」。

en: Any of several, generally large, species of birds in the genus Corvus with lustrous black plumage; especially the common raven (Corvus co…
A jet-black, often glossy, colour, like that of the plumage of a raven (etymology 1, noun sense 1).
Of the jet-black and often glossy colour of the plumage of a raven (etymology 1, noun sense 1).
To absorb or take in (something, such as information) greedily; also, to approach or pounce on (someone) like prey.

raven.ety: From Middle English raven, reven (“raven (Corvus corax); carrion crow (Corvus corone); rook (Corvus frugilegus) (?); the constellation Corvus; gall nuts of the Aleppo oak (Quercus infectoria) used to make black ink”), from Old English hræfn (“raven”), from Proto-West Germanic *hrabn (“raven”), from Proto-Germanic *hrabnaz (“raven”), probably from Proto-Indo-European *ḱrep- (“to crackle; to rattle”) or *ḱer- (“to croak, crow”), probably ultimately onomatopoeic, referring to the bird’s call.

ex.en: The raven is black.
ex.ja: カラスは黒い。

ex.ja: それはね、カラスじゃないよ。ワタリガラスだよ。

ex.en: It isn't a crow. It's a raven.
ex.ja: それはね、カラスじゃないよ。ワタリガラスだよ。

note.ja: 古英語 hræfn から。鳴き声を表す擬音的な語とされる。crow より大きなカラス。

en: A protein on a cell wall that binds with specific molecules so that they can be absorbed into the cell in order to control certain functi…
Any specialized cell or structure that responds to sensory stimuli.

receptor.ety: From Middle English receptour, from Old French receptour or Latin receptōrius, from recipiō (“receive”), from re- (“back”) + capiō (“to hold”).

ex.en: Researchers Identify New Receptor Complex in Brain
ex.ja: 研究者は頭脳の新しい受容器の複合体を識別する。

note.ja: ラテン語 receptor（受け取る者）から。recipere（受け取る）。「受容体」。receive と同じ。

An institution for rehabilitation.
To rehabilitate.

note.ja: rehabilitation の短縮。re + habilitare（能力を与える）。ability と同系。

The relation of sharing properties.

note.ja: similar（似ている）+ -ity。「類似点」。

en: One who speaks as the voice of another person or a group of people.

spokesman.ety: From spoke (“past participle of speak”) + -s- + man.

ex.en: The spokesman confirmed that the report was true.
ex.ja: スポークスマンはその報告は真実であると確認した。

ex.en: Who will act as spokesman?
ex.ja: 誰が代弁者になるか。

ex.en: The spokesman explained the blueprint of the scheme to the press.
ex.ja: 報道担当官がその計画の青写真を報道陣に説明した。

note.ja: spoke（speak の過去形）+ man。「代わりに話す人」→「報道官」。

en: A discolored spot or area caused by spillage or other contact with certain fluids or substances.
A blemish on one's character or reputation.
To discolor, as by spilling or other contact with a fluid or substance.
To taint or tarnish someone's character or reputation

en: A compartment for a single animal in a stable or cattle shed.
A stable; a place for cattle.
To put (an animal, etc.) in a stall.
To fatten.

stall.ety: From Middle English stall, stalle, from Old English steall (“standing place, position”), from Proto-Germanic *stallaz, from Proto-Indo-European *stel- (“to place, put, post, stand”). Cognate with French étal, Italian stallo, German Stall, Swedish stall.

ex.en: Stall for time until the boss gets here.
ex.ja: 上司が来るまで時間を稼いでくれ。

ex.en: Can I have a seat in the stalls?
ex.ja: 最前列の席は有りますか。

ex.en: He pushed the stalled car with all his might.
ex.ja: 彼はエンストの車を力一杯押した。

note.ja: 古英語 steall（立つ場所・馬屋）から。stand と同じ祖先。「仕切り」→「屋台・売店」、動けなくなる →「エンストする」。install（据える）も同じ。

en: starvation
Extremely hungry

ex.en: I'm starving. When the hell do we eat?
ex.ja: もう腹ペコだ。いったいいつになったら食べられるんだ。

ex.en: You must be starving now after your long walk.
ex.ja: 長い間歩いたのでハラペコでしょう。

ex.en: I saw many people starving to death on TV.
ex.ja: 私は大勢の人が餓死して行くのをテレビで見た。

note.ja: starve（飢える）+ -ing。starve は古英語 steorfan（死ぬ）。「飢えている」→（口語）「腹ぺこの」。

en: A long, narrow, pliable strip of leather, cloth, or the like.
A strap worn on the shoulder.
To beat or chastise with a strap; to whip, to lash.
To fasten or bind with a strap.

ex.en: Tom is a strapping young man.
ex.ja: トムは逞しい青年だ。

ex.en: He is a strapping man.
ex.ja: 彼は逞しい男だ。

note.ja: strop（革ひも）の変化形。ラテン語 struppus（ひも）。「ひも・ストラップ」。

The subjective case.
A noun or pronoun in the subjective case.

subjective.ety: From Latin subiectīvus, equivalent to subject + -ive.

ex.en: His writing is very subjective.
ex.ja: 彼の文章はとても主観的だ。

note.ja: subject（主体）+ -ive。「主観的な」。objective の対。

en: Of, caused by, or causing trauma.
Produced by wounds, especially as opposed to disease or other process.

traumatic.ety: From the Latin traumaticus, from the Ancient Greek τραυματικός (traumatikós), from τραῦμα (traûma). By surface analysis, trauma + -tic.

note.ja: trauma（心の傷）+ -tic。ギリシャ語 trauma（傷）。「心に傷を残す」。

en: A million (times a) million: 1 followed by twelve zeros, 10¹².
An unspecified very large number.

trillion.ety:

ex.en: I wish Tatoeba had 10 trillion example sentences.
ex.ja: タトエバに10兆例文があれば良いのに。

note.ja: tri（3）+ million。もとは「100万の3乗」の意。アメリカ式では 10の12乗 →「1兆」。billion も同じ作り。

en: A person or a company that vends or sells.
A vending machine.
To bundle third-party dependencies with the source code for one's own program.
As the software vendor, to bundle one's own, possibly modified version of dependencies with a standard program.

vendor.ety: Borrowed from Anglo-Norman vendor (Old French vendeor), from Latin venditor (“seller”), from vendere (“to sell, cry up for sale, praise”), contraction of venundare, venumdare, also, as originally, two words venum dare (“to sell”), from venum (“sale, price”) + dare (“to give”).

ex.en: There are also vendors who support Linux.
ex.ja: リナックスをサポートしているベンダーもいます。

ex.en: The ice cream vendor is waiting on customers at his outdoor stand.
ex.ja: アイスクリーム売りが外の売店で客にアイスクリームを売っている。

note.ja: vend（売る）+ -or。ラテン語 vendere（売る）。「売り手」。vending machine と同じ。

An animal or plant native to a region.

The process of adjusting a mechanism such that its parts are aligned; the condition of having its parts so adjusted.

ex.en: My side mirror is out of alignment.
ex.ja: サイドミラーがまっすぐになっていない。

en: Perfect happiness.
To feel bliss; (by extension) to reach a state of bliss or ecstasy.

bliss.ety: From Middle English bliss, from Old English bliss, variant of earlier blīds, blīþs (“joy, gladness”), from Proto-West Germanic *blīþisi (“joy, goodness, kindness”).

ex.ja: これ以上の幸せはないと思った。

ex.ja: 彼らの結婚生活は幸福で満たされていた。

ex.en: The bliss was often interrupted by anxiety.
ex.ja: 至福の時はしばしば不安に妨げられた。

note.ja: 古英語 bliss（喜び）から。blithe（陽気な）と同じ祖先。「至福」。

en: Of, relating to, or concerning the body.
Having a body or material form; physical; corporeal.
In bodily form; physically, corporally.
Pertaining to the whole body or mass; wholly.

bodily.ety: From Middle English bodily; equivalent to body + -ly.

ex.ja: 父親は息子の体をかついで部屋から運び出した。

ex.ja: 眠ると体の機能がゆっくりになり、体温が下がる。

ex.ja: 寝ている間は、体の機能は不活発になり、体温は下がる。

en: A machine with rotary brushes, passed over a hard floor to clean it.
A machine for polishing shoes and boots.
To use a buffer or buffers; to attempt to isolate or minimize the effects of one thing or another.
To queue up (an input) so that it is performed immediately once it is possible.

ex.ja: 外国人労働者は日本経済のバッファーであってはならない。

ex.ja: 彼らは枯木を全部切り倒した。

An organized group of people or entities who collaborate towards a particular goal.

en: To begin, start.
To begin, start.

commence.ety: From Middle English commencen, comencen (also as contracted comsen, cumsen), from Anglo-Norman comencer, from Vulgar Latin *cominitiāre, formed from Latin com- + initiō (whence English initiate).

ex.en: The conference will commence in due course.
ex.ja: 会議はそのうち始まるでしょう。

ex.en: The meeting will commence.
ex.ja: 会合は午後三時から始まる。

ex.en: Direct flights between New York and Tokyo commenced recently.
ex.ja: ニューヨーク・東京間の直行便が最近開始された。

note.ja: co（すっかり）+ initiare（始める）。「始める・始まる」。initiate と同じ。

en: To do (something good) after (something bad) happens.
To pay or reward someone in exchange for work done or some other consideration.

compensate.ety: Borrowed from Latin compēnsātus, perfect passive participle of compensō (“to weight together one thing against another, balance, make good”), -ate (verb-forming suffix) for more.

ex.en: He compensated me for the accident with money.
ex.ja: 彼はお金でその事故の補償をした。

ex.en: I worked hard to compensate for the loss.
ex.ja: 私は損害を埋め合わせするために一生懸命働いた。

ex.ja: 君は彼に彼がなくしたお金を戻すべきだ。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pens（量る）+ ate。釣り合うように量る →「補償する・埋め合わせる」。

en: Relating to or causing construction.
Carefully considered and meant to be helpful.

constructive.ety: From Latin cōnstrūctīvus. By surface analysis, construct + -ive.

ex.ja: 前向きにご検討下さい。

ex.ja: 君の意見はとても建設的だ。

en: Free from a duty, obligation, rule, law, etc.
Not entitled to overtime pay when working overtime.

ex.ja: ５万円未満の場合は、非課税になります。

ex.ja: この品物は全部免税です。

ex.ja: ５万円未満の場合は、非課税になります。

ex.ja: 彼女は気を失ったが五分ぐらいで回復した。

The birthrate of a population; the number of live births per 1000 people per year.

ex.ja: 排卵誘発剤を使っています。

en: A national of Finland.
A person of ethnic Finnish (Suomi) ancestry; a non-Swedish, non-Sami Finlander.

Finn.ety: From Old English Finnas (“the Sami”) (plural), from Old Norse finnr (“a hunter-gatherer”), from Proto-Germanic *finnaz (which see for more). Possibly originally meaning a ‘finder’ of food, referring to nomadic hunter-gatherers, particularly the Sami.

ex.en: Finns drink a lot of coffee.
ex.ja: フィンランド人はコーヒーをたくさん飲みます。

To form or emit foam.
To spew saliva as foam; to foam at the mouth.

ex.ja: ビールは泡立ってコップから溢れた。

ex.en: The sea was white with foam.
ex.ja: 波は白波が立っていた。

ex.en: The breaking waves formed foam.
ex.ja: くだける波が泡を作った。

note.ja: 古英語 fām（泡）から。「泡・泡立つ」。

Coming before (all) others in time.

First in time.

ex.ja: 何よりもまず、食事に気をつけなさい。

ex.en: I told it to my mother first and foremost.
ex.ja: 私は真っ先に母にそれを告げた。

note.ja: 古英語 formest（最も前の）から。fore（前）の最上級。「第一の・真っ先に」。

en: A furnace or hearth where metals are heated prior to hammering them into shape.
A workshop in which metals are shaped by heating and hammering them.
To shape a metal by heating and hammering.
To form or create with concerted effort.

ex.en: He forged the steel into a sword.

A structure that shields the operating table to protect against bacteria.
To place (plants) in a greenhouse.

Richly supplied; wealthy; possessing in great quantity.

ex.ja: 米国は天然資源に富んでいる。

ex.ja: その地方は天然資源に富む。

ex.ja: 日本は天然資源に富んでいない。

ex.ja: 代数の苦手な生徒が多い。

ex.en: Algebra is a branch of mathematics.
ex.ja: 代数は数学の１部門です。

Discovery, interpretation, and communication of meaningful patterns in data.

analytics.ety: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἀναλυτικά (analutiká, “science of analysis”).

note.ja: analytic（分析の）+ -s。analysis と同じ。ギリシャ語 analyein（ほどく）。

en: An appendage used for sensing on the head of an insect, crab, or other animal.
An apparatus to receive or transmit electromagnetic waves and convert respectively to or from an electrical signal.

antenna.ety: Borrowed from Latin antenna, antemna (“yard, sailyard; pole”). First used in this sense as a Latin word in the 15th century and as an English word by the end of the 17th century.

ex.en: The man tried to install his own antenna.
ex.ja: その男はアンテナを取り付けようとした。

ex.en: You'll get a clear picture with this antenna on the roof.
ex.ja: このアンテナを屋根につけると画面がはっきりする。

ex.ja: テレビアンテナが昨夜のあらしでとれた。

The sense of hearing.
To evaluate one or more performers in through an audition.
To take part in such a performance.

ex.ja: 彼女は先週オーディションを受けた。

ex.ja: 「お見事、よくやった」と小川選手を褒め称える報道が多かった。

note.ja: イタリア語 bravo（勇敢な・すばらしい）から。brave と同じ語源。

en: A cut of meat, often containing a section of a rib.
A blow with an axe, cleaver, or similar implement.
To cut into pieces with short, vigorous cutting motions.
To sever with an axe or similar implement.

Grateful or indebted because of a favor done.

ex.en: She was obliged to marry the old man.
ex.ja: 彼女はその老人と結婚せざるをえなかった。

ex.en: We were obliged to give up our plan.
ex.ja: われわれは計画をあきらめなければならなかった。

ex.en: She was obliged to give up the plan.
ex.ja: 彼女はやむを得ずその計画をあきらめた。

note.ja: oblige（義務を負わせる）+ -ed。ob + ligare（縛る）。「縛られた」→「義務がある・恩を受けた」。

en: An actual instance when a situation occurs; an event or happening.
The lexical aspect (aktionsart) of verbs or predicates that change in or over time.

occurrence.ety: From Middle French occurrence, from Medieval Latin occurrentia. Morphologically occur + -ence.

ex.en: That is the common occurrence in Japan.
ex.ja: それは日本ではありきたりの出来事だ。

ex.en: This is a daily occurrence.
ex.ja: こんな出来事は日常茶飯である。

ex.en: Needless to say, it was a rare occurrence.
ex.ja: 言うまでもありませんが、それは滅多にないことでした。

note.ja: occur（起こる）+ -ence。ob + currere（走る）。「（心に）走ってくる」→「出来事・発生」。current と同じ cur。

en: A person's daughter or son; a person's child.
Any of a person's descendants, including of further generations.

offspring.ety: From Middle English ofspring, from Old English ofspring (“offspring, descendants, posterity”), equivalent to off- + spring. Compare Icelandic afspringur (“offspring”). More at off, spring.

ex.en: What will become of our offspring if a nuclear war breaks out?
ex.ja: もし核戦争になったら、われわれの子孫はどうなるのでしょう。

ex.en: These legends should be handed down to our offspring.
ex.ja: これらの伝説は私達の子孫に語り継がれるべきだ。

ex.en: Some animals are producing offspring in zoos.
ex.ja: 動物園で子を生んでいる動物もいる。

note.ja: off（離れて）+ spring（生じる）。「〜から生じたもの」→「子・子孫」。

en: Violating morality or decency; provoking indignation or affront.
Transgressing reasonable limits; extravagant, immoderate.

outrageous.ety: From Anglo-Norman outrageus, Middle French outrageus, from outrage; equivalent to outrage + -ous.

ex.en: It is outrageous that you should spend so much money.
ex.ja: 君がそんなにお金を使うとはあきれるばかりだ。

note.ja: outrage（暴挙）+ -ous。古フランス語 outre（度を越して）、ラテン語 ultra。「度を越した」→「とんでもない」。

en: A small pack or package; a little bundle or parcel
Originally, a vessel employed by government to convey dispatches or mails; hence, a vessel employed in conveying dispatches, mails, passe…
To make up into a packet or bundle.
To send in a packet or dispatch vessel.

packet.ety: From Middle English pacquet; either from Middle French pacquet, or formed independently from pak and -et.

ex.en: How many packets of cigarettes do you smoke a day?
ex.ja: タバコ、一日に何箱吸ってるの？

ex.en: This instant soup comes in individual packets.
ex.ja: このインスタントスープは１つ１つ包みの中に入っている。

note.ja: pack（包み）+ -et（小さい）。「小さな包み」→「小袋・パケット」。

en: A footpath or other path or track.
A sequence of biochemical compounds, and the reactions linking them, that describe a process in metabolism or catabolism.

pathway.ety: From Middle English pathwei, equivalent to path + way. Cognate with German Pfadweg, Afrikaans padweg.

ex.en: Most important of all, the brain needs global reentry pathways connecting these anatomical structures.
ex.ja: もっとも重要なことは、脳にはこれらの解剖学的組織を結合する全体的な再入経路が必要である。

note.ja: path（小道）+ way（道）。「小道・経路」。

en: Any tree of species Prunus persica, native to China and now widely cultivated throughout temperate regions, having pink flowers and edibl…
Soft juicy stone fruit of the peach tree, having yellow flesh, downy, red-tinted yellow skin, and a deeply sculptured pit or stone contai…
Of or pertaining to the color peach.
Particularly pleasing or agreeable.

Medieval Latin pesca) from Late Latin persica, from Classical Latin mālum persicum, from Ancient Greek μᾶλον περσικόν (mâlon persikón, “Persian apple”). Displaced Middle English persogȝe, from Old English persoc, ultimately from the same Latin root above.

ex.en: The colour peach is a cute colour, isn't it?
ex.ja: 桃色って、可愛い色だよね？

ex.en: The colour peach is cute, isn't it?
ex.ja: 桃色って、可愛い色だよね？

ex.en: Peach is a cute colour, isn't it?
ex.ja: 桃色って、可愛い色だよね？

note.ja: ラテン語 persicum malum（ペルシャのりんご）から。「桃」。

en: A ball game where two teams of players on horseback use long-handled mallets to propel the ball along the ground and into their opponent'…
The game of ice polo, one of the ancestors of ice hockey; a similar game played on the ice, or on a prepared floor, by players wearing sk…
To play the game of polo.

polo.ety: From Balti پولو (polo, “ball”). Cognate with Tibetan པོ་ལོ (po lo), ཕོ་ལོང (pho long), སྤོ་ལོ (spo lo, “ball”).

ex.en: Tom was wearing a polo shirt.
ex.ja: トムはポロシャツを着てたよ。

ex.en: When I was in high school, I played water polo in gym class.
ex.ja: 私は高校生の頃、体育の授業で水球をした。

ex.en: Sami formed his own polo team.
ex.ja: サミは自分のポロチームを作った。

note.ja: チベット語 pulu（ボール）から。「ポロ（競技）」→ 選手の着るシャツ →「ポロシャツ」。

en: To announce or declare.

proclaim.ety: From Middle English proclamen, proclaime, from Old French proclamer, from Latin prōclāmō, prōclāmāre, from prō- (“forth”) + clāmō (“to shout, cry out”). Spelling altered by influence of claim, from the same Latin source (clāmō).

ex.en: Iran proclaimed war against the US.
ex.ja: イランはアメリカ合衆国に対して宣戦布告をした。

ex.en: The law came into effect on the day it was proclaimed.
ex.ja: その法律は即日施行された。

ex.en: His manners proclaim him a gentleman.
ex.ja: 彼の礼儀作法を見れば彼が紳士であることが分かる。

note.ja: pro（前で）+ claim（叫ぶ）。人前で叫ぶ →「宣言する・公表する」。

en: An act of prohibiting, forbidding, disallowing, or proscribing something.
A law prohibiting the manufacture or sale of alcohol.

prohibition.ety: From Anglo-Norman and Old French prohibicion, from Latin prohibitiō. By surface analysis, prohibit + -ion.

ex.en: The first prohibition of slavery was in the mid-nineteenth century.
ex.ja: 初めての奴隷制度禁止令は１９世紀半ばに行われた。

note.ja: prohibit（禁止する）+ -ion。pro（前で）+ habere（持つ）。「前に立ちはだかる」→「禁止」→ 米国の「禁酒法」。

en: An object placed against or under another, to support it; anything that supports.
The player on either side of the hooker in a scrum.
To support or shore up something.
To play rugby in the prop position.

prop.ety: From Middle English proppe (“a prop, support, support for a vine or plant”), from Middle Dutch proppe (“support, support for a vine, stopper for a bottle”). Compare Middle Low German proppe (“plug, stopper”), German Pfropfen (“plug”), Danish prop (“plug, stopper”).

ex.en: He propped his bike against the wall.
ex.ja: 彼は自転車を壁に立てかけた。

ex.en: He fetched a few cushions to prop up her head.
ex.ja: 彼は頭をのせるため二三のクッションを持ってきた。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 proppe（支柱）から。「支え」。劇の「小道具」は property の短縮で別語。

en: A building in which things are registered or where registers are kept.
A record; an account; a register.

registry.ety: A variant of registery, from Middle English regestery (“?a record book; ?a bookmark”), partly from Medieval Latin regesterium, registerium and probably also partly formed with -ery. Equivalent to register + -y.

note.ja: register（登録する）+ -ry。ラテン語 regerere（書き留める）、re + gerere（運ぶ）。「登録所・登記簿」。

en: To ease (a person, person's thoughts etc.) from mental distress; to stop (someone) feeling anxious or worried, to alleviate the distress of.
To ease (someone, a part of the body etc.) or give relief from physical pain or discomfort.

relieve.ety: From Late Middle English releven, from Old French relever, specifically from the conjugated forms such as (jeo) relieve (“I lift up”), and its source, Latin relevo (“to lift up, lighten, relieve, alleviate”), combined form of re- (“back”) + levo (“to lift”). Doublet of relevate. Compare levant, levity, etc.

ex.en: He contributed much money to relieving the poor.
ex.ja: 彼は貧民救済に多額のお金を寄付した。

ex.en: Let me relieve you of that case.
ex.ja: そのケースを運ばせてください。

ex.en: I wish you to relieve me of my anxiety.
ex.ja: 私から心配を取り除いてほしい。

note.ja: re（再び）+ levare（持ち上げる・軽くする）。「重荷を軽くする」→「和らげる・安心させる」。relief、lever と同じ lev。

en: In a remarkable manner.
To a noteworthy extent.

remarkably.ety:
Etymology tree
English remarkable
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English remarkably
From remarkable + -ly.

ex.en: She is remarkably attractive.
ex.ja: 彼女は並外れて魅力的だ。

ex.en: My father aged remarkably during his convalescence.
ex.ja: 父は病後、めっきり老け込んでしまった。

ex.en: Production has remarkably increased.
ex.ja: 生産高が著しく増加した。

note.ja: remarkable（注目すべき）+ -ly。re（強く）+ mark（印をつける）。「目立つほど」→「著しく」。

en: undergoing physical rotation
that proceeds in sequence or in turns

note.ja: rotate（回転する）+ -ing。ラテン語 rota（車輪）。「回転する・交代制の」。

en: A permanent mark on the skin, sometimes caused by the healing of a wound.
A permanent negative effect on someone's mind, caused by a traumatic experience.
To mark the skin permanently.
To form a scar.

scar.ety:
From Middle English scar, scarre, a conflation of Old French escare (“scab”) (from Late Latin eschara, from Ancient Greek ἐσχάρα (eskhára, “scab left from a burn”), and thus a doublet of eschar) and Middle English skar (“incision, cut, fissure”) (from Old Norse skarð (“notch, chink, gap”), from Proto-Germanic *skardaz (“gap, cut, fragment”)). Akin to Old Norse skor (“notch, score”), Old English sċeard (“gap, cut, notch”). More at shard.
Displaced native Old English dolg, dolgswæþ, and wundswaþu (“scar”). Not related to scarify.

ex.en: Tom showed Mary the scar on his leg.
ex.ja: トムは足の傷跡をメアリーに見せた。

ex.en: The wound in the arm left a scar.
ex.ja: 腕の傷は跡を残した。

ex.en: The scar on his cheek hardly shows now.
ex.ja: 彼のほおの傷あとは今ではほとんどわからない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 eskhara（かさぶた）から。「傷跡」。

en: A sacred writing or holy book.
An authoritative statement.

From Middle English scripture, from Latin scrīptūra (“a writing, scripture”), from scrīptum, the supine of scrībō (“to write”). By surface analysis, script + -ure.

ex.en: The problem is one of interpreting these ancient scriptures.
ex.ja: これは古代の教典を解釈するという問題である。

ex.en: Then they believed the scripture and the words that Jesus had spoken.
ex.ja: 聖書とイエスが言われた言葉を信じた。

ex.en: The Koran is Islamic scripture.
ex.ja: コーランはイスラム教徒の聖典です。

note.ja: ラテン語 scriptura（書かれたもの）から。scribere（書く）。「聖典」。script と同じ scrib。

en: A class held for advanced studies in which students meet regularly to discuss original research, under the guidance of a professor.
A meeting held for the exchange of useful information by members of a common business community.
To participate in or lead a seminar.

seminar.ety: From German Seminar, from Latin sēminārium, from sēmen (“seed”). Compare seminary.

ex.en: Pretty good. Did you go to today's history seminar?
ex.ja: とてもいいわ、今日の歴史のセミナーには行ったの？

ex.en: This seminar will target senior marketing leaders from Japanese firms.
ex.ja: このセミナーは、日本企業のマーケティング担当管理職を対象としたものです。

ex.en: We hope that you will be able to join us at this seminar.
ex.ja: あなたがこのセミナーに参加してくださること願っています。

note.ja: ドイツ語 Seminar から。ラテン語 seminarium（苗床）、semen（種）。「学問の苗床」→「セミナー・ゼミ」。

en: The quality or state of being unmixed or uncompounded
The quality or state of being not complex, or of consisting of few parts.

simplicity.ety: From Middle English simplicite, from Old French simplicite, from Latin simplicitās, from simplex (“simple”). See simple. By surface analysis, simple + -icity. Partially displaced native English onefoldness.

ex.en: I like the simplicity of her dress.
ex.ja: 私は彼女のドレスのシンプルなところが好きだ。

ex.en: His story was simplicity itself.
ex.ja: 彼の話は単純そのものであった。

note.ja: simple + -icity。「簡単さ・素朴さ」。

en: In a soft manner; gently.
Not loudly; nearly inaudibly.

softly.ety: From Middle English softely, softeliche, equivalent to soft + -ly.

ex.en: Mr Smith is a softly-spoken person.
ex.ja: スミスさんはソフトな語り口の人物です。

ex.en: The mother laid her baby on the bed softly.
ex.ja: その母親は赤ちゃんをそっとベッドに横たえた。

ex.en: You speak so softly that I cannot quite hear what you say.
ex.ja: あなたはとても静かにお話しになるので、私にはおっしゃることがよく聞こえません。

note.ja: soft（柔らかい）+ -ly。「そっと・静かに」。

en: An individual instance that represents a class; an example.
A banknote printed for distribution to central banks to aid in the recognition of banknotes from a country other than their own

specimen.ety: From Latin specimen (“mark, sign, example”), from speciō (“observe, watch”).

ex.en: This is a very rare specimen.
ex.ja: これは大変珍しい例だ。

ex.en: These specimens are divided into several categories.
ex.ja: これらの標本はいくつかの種類に分類される。

ex.en: A good specimen might weigh up to a kilo.
ex.ja: いいものになると１キロにもなるものがありますよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 specimen（見本）から。specere（見る）。「見るためのもの」→「標本・見本」。spectacle と同じ spec。

A stereotype.
Of sound, music, etc, recorded in stereo.
Of a pair of images: one depicting the view as would be seen from one eye and the other from the other eye, so that when viewed appropria…
To create a stereophotographic image of.

stereo.ety: A shortened form of stereotype, stereoscope or stereophonic, all originally derived, via stereo-, from Ancient Greek στερεός (stereós, “solid”).

ex.en: Would you turn down the stereo a little?
ex.ja: 少しステレオの音を小さくしてください。

ex.en: I got a new stereo at that store.
ex.ja: 私はあの店で新しいステレオを買った。

ex.en: Something seems to be wrong with the stereo set.
ex.ja: このステレオは、どこか故障しているようです。

note.ja: stereophonic の短縮。ギリシャ語 stereos（立体の・固い）+ phōnē（音）。「立体的な音」。
